html:
A Bronze Age culture of the Pontic steppe, north of the Black Sea, from about 2500 to 1950 BCE. The map shows it in 2000 BCE.

It grew out of the Yamnaya culture and kept its herding life and its kurgan mounds. What set it apart was the grave: a shaft dug down, with a side chamber, the catacomb, cut out for the body. Some burials have clay masks modelled over the skull, and some hold wagons. Its people kept cattle and sheep, used horses, and traded with the metal-working peoples of the North Caucasus.

On the steppe it was followed by the Multi-cordoned Ware culture and then the Srubnaya culture, while further east the Sintashta and Andronovo cultures developed the light chariot. Some scholars link the Catacomb people to the spread of Indo-European languages, toward the Balkans or among the ancestors of the Indo-Iranians, but this is debated.
sum: A Bronze Age culture of the Pontic steppe, north of the Black Sea, from about 2500 to 1950 BCE. The map shows it in 2000 BCE.
